title: Hook
text: An octopus has roughly five hundred million neurons, but most of them are not in its head. They are in its arms.
nxt: How can an animal think with its whole body?

title: Donut Brain
text: In humans, most of the thinking happens in the central brain, protected inside the skull.
nxt: In the octopus, only about one-third of the neurons sit in the central brain, which wraps around the esophagus like a donut.

title: Local Minds
text: This means each arm has its own local nervous system that can make simple decisions. If an arm is cut off, it does not just go limp.
nxt: For a while, it can still react to touch, pull away from harmful stimuli, and even grasp objects with its suckers.

title: Losing the Shell
text: Why did such a strange system evolve? Part of the story may be the shell.
nxt: The ancestors of modern octopuses gradually shrank their shell, tucked it inside the body, and in octopuses lost it almost entirely.
